content:
Computational pre-work toward Lean formalization of Erdős Problem #114

The Erdős-Herzog-Piranian conjecture asks whether z^(n−1) uniquely maximises the length of the lemniscate {z : |p(z)| = 1} among monic degree-n polynomials. Tao [2025] reduced it to a finite gap (n ≤ N₀ for some explicit N₀).

I've run dual IEEE 1788 rigorous interval arithmetic verification (Python/mpmath + Rust/inari) confirming the conjecture for 3 ≤ n ≤ 12:

  • All non-extremizer parameter boxes eliminated at level 0 for n ≥ 5
  • Dominance margins: 17.1% (n=3) to 71.4% (n=10)
  • Combined with Tao, this closes the conjecture for n ≤ 12 and n > N₀

Preprint (Zenodo): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19184467
PR to teorth/erdosproblems: https://github.com/teorth/erdosproblems/pull/260

Next step: Lean 4 formalization of the interval arithmetic certificate. Has anyone worked on formalizing IEEE 1788-style rigorous numerics in Mathlib? Pointers to relevant tactics or prior art very welcome.

See
#General announcements > LeanCert - Verified Computation & Interval Arithmetic @ 💬
#General announcements > Power series arithmetic library @ 💬
and a comparison
#general > LeanCert - Verified Computation & Interval Arithmetic @ 💬

Thanks Junyan — LeanCert is exactly the right tool here, and the Power series library is timely given the structure of our proof.

Current state: We have a Rust verifier using inari (IEEE 1788 interval arithmetic) that runs a branch-and-bound proof over the degree-n polynomial coefficient space. For each B&B box, it computes a certified real-valued upper bound L_ub(p) ≤ c for all polynomials p in that box, then checks c < L(z^n−1). This gives machine-verified, tight interval certificates for n=3..12. The scale grows fast — our frontier run for n=13 required 197 million certified interval evaluations over 15.5 hours. That's what makes question #2 below non-trivial.

I've already initialized a LeanCert project (EHP114/, pinned to mathlib v4.28.0), and the smoke tests pass. I also ran the leancert Python SDK today to confirm basic bounding on n=5 via native_decide-style kernel evaluation — lc.verify_bound(x**5 - 1, {'x': (-3.5, 3.5)}, lower=-530.0) returns certified. The EHP_n5.lean scaffold is ready but I'm not sure how to state the main bound properly.

Specific questions:

  1. Parametric certify_bound: The bound I need to certify is "for all (a₁,...,aₙ₋₁) ∈ Box, lemniscate_length(z^n + a_{n−1}z^{n−1} + ⋯) ≤ L_ub" — is certify_bound the right tactic for a bound parameterized over a coefficient vector, or does interval_roots fit better here?

  2. Certificate import: With 197M evaluations at the n=13 frontier, re-running inside Lean's kernel isn't realistic. Is there a workflow for stating the inari interval witnesses as Lean axioms (or a native_decide check at compile-time), rather than re-computing? Or does LeanCert require the computation to run inside Lean?

  3. Power series library: The arc-length integrand is |p'(γ(t))|/|p(γ(t))| integrated over the lemniscate. Is the power series library useful for bounding this integrand symbolically, or is it primarily for algebraic power series over fields?

Happy to share the full Rust verifier and the EHP114/ project if useful.
